newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge CEO backs Big Belgian Bank.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge CEO backs Big Belgian Bank.

text.p: Royale Belge chief executive officer Jean-Pierre Gerard said on Thursday he supported the idea of a large merger in the Belgian banking sector, but did not know if it would come about.
Insurer Royale Belge owns 12.4 percent of Banque Bruxelles Lambert SA which has been mooted as a partner for Generale Bank, Belgium's leading lender.

"In the Belgian market there are too many banks and none which can compete on a European level. If we can merge two to get a big bank at a European level it makes a lot of sense," Gerard told a news conference on the insurer's 1996 profit.
Gerard said Royale Belge would almost certainly want to keep a stake in any big bank conglomerate that included BBL.

"If there's a merger, it's clear that (our) stake would be diluted. We would see at that moment if we want to stay a shareholder and whether we can continue to work with them on insurance. The answer would almost certainly be positive," he said.
The merger of Royale Belge's French parent UAP with French rival AXA, creating AXA-UAP, would not change its attitude toward bancassurance. The pact is due to be completed formally in May.
"We are shareholders of BBL. We have a bancassurance agreement with them and the change at the level of AXA-UAP will not change this," Gerard said.
Royale Belge has an agreement to distribute its products with Generale Bank, which until 1996 (when it was overtaken by BBL) was the biggest banking outlet for its products.

Royale Belge forms part of a pact of shareholders in BBL comprising one of its own main shareholders, Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL), and Dexia CC, Belgium's second largest bank. Both have stakes similar in size to that of Royale Belge.
The arrangement has been challenged by European anti-trust officials, who believe it may be uncompetitive.
A European Commission official said earlier on Thursday it was still examining the agreement on the basis of documents received last month from the companies concerned.
The threat of a forced break-up has led some to speculate whether AXA-UAP, through Royale Belge, might seek to expand its interest in BBL by buying out one or both its partners.
Dexia CC has said its BBL stake is no longer strategic since it concluded its own cross border alliance with Credit Local de France last year.
Gerard said the group would have to think carefully before spending such a large amount of money. He estimated the cost of such an operation would be 40 billion Belgian francs.

"If we were to take over the GBL and Dexia stakes we might be obliged by the Banking and Finance Commission to make a full takeover bid for the bank," Royale Belge director Michel Meyfroidt added. "It's another consideration and one which we might not be in a position to consider."
Gerard said, however, that if GBL were to sell its stake in BBL, Royale Belge would not -- as a unit of GBL -- be obliged to follow, as it did in the case of Tractebel last year.
"Nothing is predetermined in this sense. Each partner is free. Each one has held its stakes since different times...and I don't know what GBL's plans are. We act separately," Gerard said.
